subject: Business
title: BATNA: Your Best Alternative
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: BATNA: Your Best Alternative.

hook.text: You're negotiating a salary but have no other job offers. The employer knows it. You have no leverage.

buildup.text: BATNA stands for Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement — your walk-away option.

discovery.text: Your power in any negotiation comes from how good your alternative is, not how strong your arguments are.

twist.text: A weak BATNA makes you desperate. A strong one makes you confident — and the other side can feel it.

climax.text: Before any negotiation, improve your BATNA first. Get another offer. Build another option.

punchline.text: The best negotiators don't beg. They have somewhere else to go.

quiz.question: What does BATNA stand for?
options: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement
Bilateral Agreement on Terms and Numbers

details.summary: BATNA, or Best Alternative to a Negotiated Agreement, is your strongest source of power in any negotiation. Developed by Fisher and Ury in Getting to Yes, BATNA defines what you will do if the current negotiation fails, setting the floor below which you should not accept any deal.
details.whyItMatters: A strong BATNA gives you the confidence to walk away from bad deals. A weak BATNA makes you desperate and vulnerable. Improving your BATNA before negotiating is often more valuable than improving your negotiation skills at the table.
takeaways: BATNA is what you will do if the current negotiation produces no agreement
A strong BATNA gives confidence to reject unfavorable terms and walk away
Improving your BATNA before negotiating increases your power at the table

faq.question: How do you improve your BATNA before entering a negotiation?
faq.answer: Generate multiple alternatives. If negotiating a job offer, have other offers in hand. If negotiating with a supplier, line up alternative suppliers. If selling a house, get multiple potential buyers. Each viable alternative strengthens your position and reduces dependence on this one deal.

faq.question: Should you reveal your BATNA to the other side?
faq.answer: Only if it is strong and credible. Revealing a strong BATNA communicates that you have options and are willing to walk away. Revealing a weak BATNA exposes vulnerability. Sometimes hinting at alternatives without full disclosure is enough to shift the dynamic in your favor.
